notes.content: DIVERSITY REQUIREMENT FOR CAL STATE LA GRADUATION

The articulation information in Assist.org not only shows a link to the admission requirements (aka our Major Specific Criteria webpage) but also Cal State LA graduation requirements that may be completed at the lower-division level, prior to transferring to the University. The diversity requirement is a graduation requirement , not an admission requirement. The diversity requirement may be completed prior to, or after, transferring to the University. For the Cal State LA degree, students will be required to complete two courses (six units) certified as diversity courses, at least one focusing on issues of race and ethnicity and their intersectionality with other social categories that structure inequality in society. These courses can be completed either at the lower-division or upper-division level from among courses satisfying GE requirements. Please view the General Education agreements on Assist.org for the lower-division courses that will meet the Diversity (d) and Race & Ethnicity (re) Requirements.

notes.content: The electrical engineering program offers instruction in the basic sciences and in engineering analysis and design. The upper-division offerings provide a flexible, broad curriculum to enable each student to match talents and interests with career objectives. The major areas of course concentrations are biomedical, circuits, communications, computers, controls, electronics, and power. The Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org . All accredited programs are required to provide the following minimum level of instruction: one year of mathematics and basic sciences; one and one-half years of engineering science and design (engineering topics); and one-half year of humanities and social sciences. The total number of units required for the Bachelor of Science degree in Electrical Engineering is 122, of which 102 units are in the major. Electrical Engineering students are required to take 48 units of General Education (GE) of which 28 units are met by courses in the major. Consult with an advisor for the specific number of units required in all areas of the degree including GE and free electives. * Note: If CHEM 1100 has been taken to meet admission criteria, CHEM 1040 is waived.
